body:
Last night on Predictable, we got one of the biggest political headlines of the year so far:
“AOC surges to the top of the 2028 Democratic field.”
The media took the bait. But was it real? The prediction markets didn’t think so, because they barely blinked.
That disconnect is the story.
A lot of people saw one poll and immediately jumped to “President AOC?” mode. Media outlets ran with it. Social media exploded. Everyone acted like the Democratic primary had suddenly transformed overnight.
But when you looked at the actual markets, where people are risking real money on these outcomes, almost nothing happened.
In fact, some traders were actually selling her position.
Headlines vs. Signals
That doesn’t mean the poll is fake. Atlas Intel is a respected pollster and nailed 2024 better than almost anyone. But one thing we try to do on this show is separate headlines from signals.
And there were some signals in this poll that deserved a closer look.
The sampling leaned heavily Democratic. The generic congressional ballot inside the same survey showed Democrats with a massive advantage that doesn’t really line up with broader polling averages right now.
That matters, because a sample tilted that far left is naturally going to produce stronger results for candidates like AOC.
The markets noticed.
And that’s really the core idea behind Predictable. One poll can dominate cable news for 24 hours. But prediction markets force people to ask a harder question:
“Would you actually put your money behind this?”
Last night’s answer from traders was pretty clear.
Also on Last Night’s Show…
We also got into AOC’s comments claiming billionaires can’t “earn” their wealth, why that argument falls apart pretty quickly, and one of the strangest political ads you’ll ever see: an anti-Spencer Pratt mayoral ad that might actually help Spencer Pratt.
Seriously.
